# cpanel_passenger_application (Resource)

Manages one cPanel Passenger application registration. The application directory must already exist. Destroy unregisters Passenger without deleting the directory or installing dependencies.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cpanel_git_repository" "application" {
  name                       = "Example Passenger application"
  repository_root            = "applications/example"
  delete_contents_on_destroy = false
}

resource "cpanel_passenger_application" "application" {
  name            = "example"
  path            = cpanel_git_repository.application.repository_root
  domain          = "example.com"
  base_uri        = "/application"
  deployment_mode = "production"
  enabled         = false

  environment_variables = {
    APP_ENV = "production"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The existing account domain that serves the application.
- `name` (String) The Passenger application name.
- `path` (String) The existing normalized application directory relative to the cPanel account home.

### Optional

- `base_uri` (String) The normalized URL path that mounts the application on its domain. Changing it replaces the registration because cPanel cannot edit it in place.
- `deployment_mode` (String) The Passenger deployment mode: `production` or `development`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether cPanel generates the web-server configuration for the application.
- `environment_variables` (Map of String, Sensitive) The complete set of application environment variables. cPanel replaces the full set on update, and Terraform stores values as sensitive state.

### Read-Only

- `absolute_path` (String) The absolute application path reported by cPanel.
- `dependency_commands` (Map of String) The dependency installation commands reported by cPanel for `gem`, `npm`, and `pip`. The provider never executes them.
- `nodejs` (String) The Node.js executable reported by cPanel, when present.
- `python` (String) The Python executable reported by cPanel, when present.
- `ruby` (String) The Ruby executable reported by cPanel, when present.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import cpanel_passenger_application.application example
```
